name: ripgrep-6892bc2
goal:
ignore: use byte keys for incremental parent lookups

We now store incremental directory-cache keys as OsString values to
avoid path-component hashing. On Unix, we find a cached parent by
scanning path bytes before parsing components. Cache misses fall back
to the component walk, preserving alternate path spellings and cached
ignore-file snapshots.

On Linux x86-64 against 3fce3b5, warm incremental replay over Ruff
and uv path sets improves 12–13% and 15–18%, respectively, across
default and fat-LTO builds; ignored-parent checks improve about 68%.
Paths with an internal ./ are 0.5–2.2% slower.

PR #3559

name: ripgrep-2d4fa85
goal:
ignore: skip empty absolute parent matchers (#3557)

When no ancestor above the walk root has ignore rules, we now skip
constructing an absolute path and checking parent matchers. Repository
boundaries still affect Git ignore rules, even when the repository has
no rules of its own.

On Linux x86-64 against 3fce3b5, warm incremental matching improves
13.4% and replay allocates or reallocates about half as often.
Warm-cache walks of the Ruff and uv checkouts improve 1–4%; the
cached ignored-path control is 3.3% slower.

PR #3557

name: ripgrep-c5e744c
goal:

... by deferring to `Gitignore::empty()` when there aren't any globs.

name: ripgrep-7155f64
goal:
ignore: treat dotfiles ending in a dot as hidden (#3564)

`file_name()` returned `None` for any path ending in `.` on Unix,
which was meant to cover the `.` and `..` components but also matched
real names like `.foo.`. The hidden check then found no file name and
treated those files as visible. Only a final component that is exactly
`.` or `..` has no file name now.

PR #3564

name: ripgrep-020687a
goal:
ignore,globset: increase pool capacity

When do matching inside of `ignore` or `globset`, we sometimes need a
reusable mutable scratch space for matching. To do this, we use a `Pool`
abstraction from `regex-automata` to do this heavy lifting for us.

It turns out that this can be a limiting factor in some scenarios when
gitignore matching dominates. For example, in my checkout of the
Chromium repository:

  Range (min … max):   147.6 ms … 164.5 ms    19 runs

Benchmark 2: rg-bigger-pool -j32 --files
  Time (mean ± σ):     131.6 ms ±   2.1 ms    [User: 1628.2 ms, System: 310.1 ms]
  Range (min … max):   128.8 ms … 136.3 ms    22 runs

Benchmark 3: rg-master -j32 --files --no-ignore
  Time (mean ± σ):     107.4 ms ±   1.0 ms    [User: 664.7 ms, System: 304.7 ms]
  Range (min … max):   104.9 ms … 109.6 ms    28 runs

Summary
  rg-master -j32 --files --no-ignore ran

name: ripgrep-435f59f
goal:
ignore: skip loading unreachable ignore files

When parallelism isn't used (e.g., when sorting results), then
it's possible in some cases for the `ignore` crate to still try and
load gitignore files inside of directories that are never
descended into. This can occur when `--max-depth` is used, or
even just when a directory is skipped for some other reason.

Fixes #2565, PR #3496

name: fd-a3942db
goal:
fix: don't sanitize error message

Calling `maybe_sanitize` on error messages results in newlines getting
replaced with "\x0a". This is not desirable for error messages that have
newlines.

I audited everwhere we construct an error, and call print_error and
confirmed that none of those places have inputs that include found
paths. I'm not too worried about inputs that come from command line
arguments.

This bug was introduced in 92c54d37c0a3425b4d8b25dd8c9e4ddbbecfbe0a.

Fixes: #2104

name: fd-b3a8ff6
goal:
Take the broken symlink depth from the walker

The depth of a broken symlink was derived from its path by stripping the
matching search root, because the walker did not report a depth on the
errors that carry broken symlinks. ignore 0.4.28 fills that depth in, so
read it from the error instead and drop the path arithmetic.

The path based version could not express one case. When two search roots
overlap, the walker visits the same broken symlink once per root at a
different depth each time, and both visits carry the same path, so a
single path derived answer had to serve both. Searching roots a and a/b
with --min-depth 2 dropped a/b/blink even though a real file in its place
was kept.

name: fd-68edfde
goal:
Use a struct-like variant for broken symlinks and test max/exact depth

Address review feedback. Make DirEntryInner::BrokenSymlink a struct-like
variant with named path and depth fields, so the recorded depth is clear
at every use site. Add regression tests that a broken symlink is filtered
by --max-depth and --exact-depth the same way a normal entry is, both
through the real directory tree and through a followed symlink.

name: fd-4a89aff
goal:
Make broken symlink depth robust under absolute paths

The depth for a broken symlink was derived by stripping the search root
from its path and counting the remaining components. Compare the path
and the roots in absolute form before stripping, so the match holds
whether or not --absolute-path has already made the roots absolute, and
pick the deepest matching root. This avoids an absolute path failing to
match a relative root and falling back to an inflated depth.

Add a regression test that exercises the broken symlink case together
with --absolute-path.

name: hono-ae401f0
goal:
fix(css): keep the descendant combinator before a pseudo-class when minifying (#5451)

The minifier removed whitespace on both sides of ":", so in a nested
selector the space that means "descendant" was lost:

  & :first-child { margin: 0 }   ->  &:first-child{margin:0}
  .a :is(h1, h2) { color: red }  ->  .a:is(h1,h2){color:red}

That rule then matches the element itself instead of its descendants.
Only the whitespace after ":" is removed now.
